A.claim: Whenever 3|x, 3|y and 3|z, A^x + B^y = C^z has no positive solutions; in particular no Beal counterexample has such a signature, including the Fermat cubic (3,3,3).

B.claim: Sharp curvature separation. Every hyperbolic Beal signature has |chi| >= 1/12 with equality exactly at permutations of (3,3,4), while every one of the ten known primitive hyperbolic solutions has |chi| <= 1/18. Hence Beal is equivalent to: no primitive solution has |chi| >= 1/12. This explains the exponent-2 phenomenon quantitatively - an exponent
